glosses: to get something from eating (e.g. a fat belly)

examples.text: War das eine Maus, die den Käse angefressen hat?

glosses: beginnen, etwas langsam zu zersetzen, die Struktur zu zerstören

examples.text: Der Rost hat unser schmiedeeisernes Tor schon angefressen.
Die großen Geldsorgen fraßen seine Seele an.

glosses: sich etwas durch (vieles/übermäßiges) Fressen zuziehen, bekommen (zum Beispiel ein Fettpolster/einen Bauch)
tags: reflexiv, von Tieren, derb von Menschen

examples.text: Na, du hast dir ja eine ganz schöne Wampe angefressen!

„Um den Wasserfall zu überwinden, schwimmen die Lachse an das untere Ende des Falls und springen dann nach oben – manche landen dabei direkt in den Fängen der Bären, die sich vor dem Winterschlaf noch eine angenehme Fettschicht anfressen wollen.“

glosses: bis zur völligen Sättigung oder Übersättigung fressen

examples.text: Heute bekam der Zoo eine große Fleischlieferung vom Schlachthof, da dürfen sich die Raubkatzen anfressen.

translations.source_sense_description: von Tieren, derb von Menschen: ein Stückchen von etwas fressen
übertragen: beginnen, etwas langsam zu zersetzen, die Struktur zu zerstören

glosses: To wear away by abrasion, corrosion, or chemical reaction.

examples.text: The cliff is gradually being eroded by the waves.

glosses: To destroy gradually by an ongoing process.

examples.text: to erode a person’s trust
to erode society’s morals

translations.source_sense_description: übertragen: jemanden verärgern, im Inneren angreifen

examples.text: stylistic peeve
He was peeved to note that his hard work had been undone.
The motor bogies are built up from plates and rolled sections, and have cast-steel, one-piece axleguards, with manganese liners.
to build up a door

glosses: To accumulate: to increase incrementally or continually.

examples.text: Ever since the secretary left, the letters in my inbox have started to build up.

The first English Electric units were not fitted with an anti-slip brake, but a hurried consultation of the wiring diagram showed that it should be possible to hold in the low-voltage anti-slip relay for long enough to let speed build up without cutting off the motor current.
Their first half was marred by the entire side playing too deep, completely unable to build up any form of decent possession once the ball left their bewildered defence.
As we age, the major arteries of our bodies frequently become thickened with plaque, a fatty material with an oatmeal-like consistency that builds up along the inner lining of blood vessels.
They had to build up their fortress to protect against attack.
"It took it out of me, though. I'm a rag this morning." "They work you too hard, dear. I'll take you to Margate and build you up." "Well, maybe at Easter we could do a week."

glosses: In solitaire card games, to place a card over another card of lower value. (e.g., place 5♦ over 4♣)

glosses: Heavy, dull, often starchy food, such as a steamed pudding

examples.text: The meal was nothing but heavy stodge with no fresh vegetables.
After weeks of bread and porridge, he longed for something other than stodge.
Critics dismissed the book as academic stodge.
